mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility (t-3w to t-0w: -56.3 to -37.3, a 19-point gain) signals normalization of commuting patterns. This restores weekday retail foot traffic and consumer confidence, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 19 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 10 points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility (t-3w to t-0w: -20.9 to 19.3, a 40-point swing into positive territory) indicates outdoor activity substitution is saturating. Consumers redirect discretionary spending from parks back to indoor retail and recreation venues, accelerating RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses zero and remains positive for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility declines below +5 in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to accelerate relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (t-0w: -44.3), constraining access to retail districts. If TRANSIT does not recover by at least 15 points within two weeks, RETAIL_REC will stall or decline because commuter-dependent retail clusters remain inaccessible.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers by more than 15 points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises despite TRANSIT stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are jointly constrained by mobility restrictions. When both series show synchronized recovery (GROCERY_PHARM: -26.4 to -10.0, a 16-point gain), it signals lifting of access barriers. This dual recovery interaction predicts accelerated RETAIL_REC growth as consumers resume discretionary shopping alongside essential trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both improve by at least 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent four-week improvement
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC diverge (one rises, one falls) in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC growth rate decelerates below 5 points per week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (t-0w: 14.9) relative to baseline, indicating stay-at-home compliance or preference persists. If RESIDENTIAL does not fall below 10 within one week, it signals ongoing restrictions that will suppress RETAIL_REC recovery despite workplace reopening.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 in week t+1
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5 in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises despite elevated RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week trajectory shows consistent RETAIL_REC recovery (-73.0 to -37.6, a 35-point gain). This linear trend, absent external shocks, will continue over the next four weeks at a decelerating rate, producing net positive RETAIL_REC change as the baseline effect compounds.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 35.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in week t+1 or t+2, or the week-on-week improvement rate falls below 5 points for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility interact: when both recover simultaneously, commuter-dependent retail clusters become accessible and populated. The interaction of workplace return (+19 points) with transit recovery (if it occurs) will amplify RETAIL_REC gains beyond either signal alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by at least 8 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered 19 points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT fails to improve by 8 points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC growth rate does not exceed 8 points per week when both proxies improve.

candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above +15 for two consecutive weeks
